title: sizes=auto images shouldn't use concrete object width to select source
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? Currently, sizes=auto lazy-loading images use the [concrete object size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#concrete-object-size) width to select which source to use (see [step 3.3 here](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/images.html#parsing-a-sizes-attribute)). This can be problematic since the concrete object size can be affected by the image's (intrinsic) aspect ratio. For example, consider ```html
``` The concrete object size of the image is initially 1000x100 before any image loads, so big.png will be selected. Then, supposing big.png has a 1:1 aspect ratio, the concrete object size will shrink to 100x100 to maintain the aspect ratio while fitting in the container due to the [object-fit: contain constraint](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#cover-contain). So now, according to the current spec, small.png must be loaded. This seems wasteful (and could even lead to an infinite loop if small.png had a 10:1 aspect ratio!). Probably it's best to use the content box width instead, and that seems to be what Blink is doing anyways if I understand correctly: https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/css/parser/sizes_attribute_parser.cc;l=148;drc=fa6d7f63f5d366cbe43509c6ded6eb75b16f5088
